chapter: Billy Pierce Studio and New York tap
title: J. D. the amateur-contest winner who emceed at the 81 Theater
summary: J. D. won first prize repeatedly at the 81 Theater and once emceed for a week, which is how Ella B. Moore found him.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah, see, like -- like something like you know a person, you know everybody in the audience, like

you were great friends, you know. And it was like telling a story really, but it was on a -- it was in activities, you see. And as I say, Slim was a great tap dancer. He was a natural, see, because he taught himself all these tap dances that he knew, and he used to win the first prizes all the time.

He won the first prize eight times at the 81 Theater on -- then the time after I was there, I mean he won the ninth time, see. He was after a record. He wanted to win ten first prizes, you see. And he was so good until one time he had to pinch hit for one of the master of ceremonies, a fellow named Johnny Jazz' cousin. He had to go to Tennessee, something. His mother got sick or something. He had to go to Tennessee.

And Slim, which was J. D., he was the South's Favorite Son, you see, and he had to finish the week out for Johnny Jazz' cousin, and he emceed the show. He was master of ceremonies of the show, and he did his tap dancing, because he had actually become a favorite at this theater, the 81 theater, you see, and it was good for him to get a chance to do this week, you see, because that's really how this woman discovered him, Ella B. Moore, you see, and got us together, see.

But then getting back to New York, he continued to be a great tap dancer, and he was always learning me things, you know, something. I say, well, what would happen if we have to do some other tap dance, and what are we going to do? And we were in the process of teaching each other how to do --
